Criteria for laying new rail lines and
gauge conversion
*421. SHRI O.T. LEPCHA: Will the
Minister of RAILWAYS be pleased to
state:
(a) the details of criteria fixed by
Government for taking up new railway
lines and gauge conversion works in the
country;
(b) whether there are railway lines yet
to be converted in broad gauge lines in NER;
and
(c) the details of steps proposed to be
taken by Government to remove the
regional imbalance in this regard?
New trains for Kerala
*422. SHRI K.E. ISMAIL: Will the
Minister of RAILWAYS be pleased to
state:
(a) whether his Ministry is aware of
the acute difficulties faced by passengers
from Kerala to various destinations and back
because of the absence of sufficient train
services; and
(b) if so, whether his Ministry would
take urgent steps to start new train services
from Thiruvananthapuram to Bangalore,
New Delhi, Mumbai and other destinations
and back to mitigate the hardships of the
passengers?
Approval for registration of products
of M/s Dow Chemicals
*423. SHRI S.S. AHLUWALIA: Will
the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have taken
cognizance of the report of disclosure made
in the 13th February, 2007 report of the
US Securities Exchange Commission (SEC)
about the confession of M/s Dow
Chemicals of having bribed Government
officials in India some years ago for securing
registration/approvals of their products;
(b) if so, whether any enquiry has been
conducted on the basis thereof;
(c) if so, the outcome thereof; and
(d) if not, the reasons therefor?

133
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Increasing the productivity of cereals
*424. SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA:
SHRI KALRAJ MISHRA:
 Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE
be pleased to state:
(a) the plan of Government to increase
the productivity of cereals, particularly
wheat and rice; and
(b) whether Government have any plan
to bring productivity to the international
level for these cereals?
Bridges awaiting rehabilitation
*425. SHRI B.J. PANDA: Will the
Minister of RAILWAYS be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that around
76,000 old railway bridges are awaiting
rehabilitation;
(b) whether at the present rate, it would
take decades to complete rehabilitation;
(c) what are the details of such bridges
on the ECoR which need rehabilitation;
and
(d) the action plan of Government to
expedite this project, to control any kind
of railway bridge mishap like that of
Bhagalpur?
Drug licensing under one umbrella
*426. SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA:
SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA:
 Will the Minister of CHEMICALS
AND FERTILIZERS be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are
contemplating a single/central licensing
autonomous body for pharmaceuticals on
the lines of the Telecom Regulatory
Authority of India;
(b) if so, whether all diverse drug
authorities like the National Pharmaceutical
Pricing Authority (NPPA), the DPCO and
the Drug and Chemicals Act, would soon
come under one umbrella; and
(c) if so, by when a final decision in this
regard is likely to be taken?
Supply of foodgrains to hostels and
welfare institutions
*427. SHRIMATI N.P. DURGA: Will
the Minister of CONSUMER AFFAIRS,
FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that there is a
scheme called Supply of Foodgrains to
Hostels and Welfare Institutions to help
the shelterless and homeless people;
(b) if so, the details of the scheme;
(c) whether this scheme is under
implementation in Andhra Pradesh;
(d) if so, the details of allocation and off
take to Andhra Pradesh during the last five
years, year-wise;
(e) whether it is also a fact that the
percentage of off take of foodgrains against
the allocation is too low since 2002-03
onwards; and
(f) if so, the reasons therefor?
Newly developed varieties of pulses
†*428. SHRI RAJ MOHINDER
SINGH MAJITHA:
DR. MURLI MANOHAR
JOSHI:
 Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that research

134

and developed varieties of pulses in order
to boost production of pulses in the
country;

developed varieties of pulses alongwith
names of such pulses and average
production rate thereof;
(c) whether it is also a fact that seeds of
such new and developed varieties of pulses
available in laboratories are not available to
farmers for production; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Food security to citizens
*429. SHRI MAHMOOD A.
MADANI:
SHRI SANTOSH
BAGRODIA:
 Will the Minister of CONSUMER
AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC
DISTRIBUTION be pleased to state:
(a) how Government plan to ensure that
every citizen in the country can get enough
food at affordable prices; and
(b) whether it is a fact that PDS is not
able to supply enough food articles to the
poorest of the poor during the last six
months?
Advertisement of soft drinks through
celebrities
*430. SHRI K. CHANDRAN PILLAI:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether pesticide residues are found
in excess in soft drinks;
(b) whether Government are aware of
the advertisements by cola companies
endorsed by celebrities claiming 100 per
cent safety to the cola consumers;
(c) if so, whether Government consider
restrictions on the publishing of such
misleading advertisements; and
(d) if so, the details thereof and if not,
the reasons therefor?
Production of fertilizers
†*431. SHRIMATI SUSHMA
SWARAJ: Will the Minister of
CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS be
pleased to state:
(a) the quantum of production of urea
and DAP in the fertilizer producing units
in the public sector;
(b) whether the production of urea and
DAP has decreased; and
(c) if so, whether it has affected the
availability of fertilizers in the country?
Scarcity of medicines in the CGHS
dispensaries
*432. SHRIMATI SYEDA  ANWARA
TAIMUR: Will the Minister of HEALTH
AND FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that there is a
scarcity of medicines/life saving drugs in
the CGHS dispensaries hospitals located
in the NCT of Delhi;
(b) whether it is also a fact that the
CGHS beneficiaries are getting medicines
that are about to expire in a month or so;
(c) if so, what are the reasons for supply
of about to expire medicines;
(d) whether Government have taken
steps to verify stocks of various medicines
that are lying in the stocks; and
(e) if so, the details thereof?

135
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Foodgrains for APL and BPL card
holders
*433. SHRI  MATILAL SARKAR:
Will the Minister of CONSUMER
AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC
DISTRIBUTION be pleased to state:
(a) the quantity of foodgrains
distributed to each APL and BPL family
through fair price shops and the price
thereof;
(b) whether it is a fact that Government
have decided to reduce the quantity for APL
families very recently;
(c) if so, the reasons therefor and the
reactions from the State Governments
thereto; and
(d) whether Government are going to
re-instate the scale reduced for those APL
families which actually cling to the side of
BPL families?
Malaria control measures
*434. SHRI MOTIUR RAHMAN:
SHRI RAJEEV
CHANDRASEKHAR:
 Will the Minister of HEALTH AND
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether malaria disease is on the
increase rather than to have come down;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor and the
steps taken to control the disease
meaningfully and to tone up malaria control
measures; and
(c) the number of persons affected by
the disease during each of the last five years
indicating the number of deaths?
Declining sex ratio
†*435. MISS ANUSUIYA UIKEY:
SHRI EKANATH K.
THAKUR:
 Will the Minister of HEALTH AND
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) the present sex ratio in the country
and the position of the country in the world
in this regard;
(b) whether it is a fact that there has
been sharp decline in sex ratio in 80 per
cent districts of the country this year;
(c) the States having sex ratio less than
national level alongwith the sex ratio in these
States;
(d) the main reasons for the decline in
sex ratio and the efforts being made by
Government to check the same;
(e) whether the existing law has been
successful in its objective of prevention of
abortion after sex determination test; and
(f) if not, whether any amendment is
being made in this law accordingly?
Plan to construct budget hotels
†*436. SHRIMATI MAYA SINGH :
Will the Minister of RAILWAYS be pleased
to state:
(a) whether his Ministry is planning to
construct 100 budget hotels throughout the
country;
(b) if so, the cities where such budget
hotels would be constructed;
(c) the amount likely to be spent per
hotel according to estimate;
(d) whether rooms for poor people
would also be constructed in such hotels;
and

(e) if so, the details thereof?
Making Alloy Steel Plant viable
*437. SHRI TAPAN KUMAR SEN:
SHRI PRASANTA
CHATTERJEE:
 Will the Minister of STEEL be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that after
completion of expansion programme of
Salem Steel Plant, Alloy Steel Plant (ASP)
at Durgapur will face a problem to sell its
stainless steel slabs in the market;
(b) if so, what is the long term plan to
install finishing facilities to process its semi-
finished product of slabs into finished
products like plates and sheets; and
(c) if not, what are the alternative plans
and investment proposals to make ASP
viable?
Quality control of bottled water
†*438. SHRI AMIR ALAM KHAN:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) the number of companies in the
country producing and selling mineral water,
State-wise;
(b) whether Government have
appointed any regulator to control quality
of bottled water;
(c) if so, whether any complaints have
been received about bottling and selling of
contaminated water by these companies;
and
(d) if so, the details thereof and action
taken thereon, State-wise?
Unified National Market for
Agriculture
*439. SHRI T.T.V. DHINAKARAN:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is proposed to set up a
unified National Market for Agriculture;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) if not, the reasons therefor?
Projects for Andhra Pradesh
*440. SHRI M.V. MYSURA
REDDY:
SHRI C. RAMACHAND-
RAIAH:
 Will the Minister of RAILWAYS be
pleased to state:
(a) the present status of ongoing railway
projects in the State of Andhra Pradesh;
(b) the details of amount allocated,
released and spent on these projects, so
far, and the estimated cost of each project;
(c) the funds allocated during the last
three years for these projects;
(d) the time schedule for completion of
these projects; and
(e) the steps taken by Government to
complete these projects in time?

740
Statutory power to a commission
looking the welfare of small and
marginal farmers
3192. SHRI SANJAY RAUT: Will the
Minister of AGRICULTURE be pleased
to state:
(a) what are the details of policy
initiative measures that have been taken or
proposed to be taken to alleviate the
sufferings of the farmers, particularly the
small and marginal ones;
(b) whether his Ministry has issued
statutory powers, to any commission so
that they take decisions for arranging funds
and providing the funds to the needy and
poor farmers against nominal interest rates;
and
(c) if not, what are the reasons therefor?
Production of onion
†3193. SHRI RAM JETHMALANI:
DR. MURLI MANOHAR
JOSHI:
Will the Minister of AGRICUL TURE
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the
production of onion in the kharif season in
2006-07 was more than that of kharif
season of previous year;
(b) if so, the facts thereof alongwith the
details of production of onion during both
of the said years, separately;
(c) whether it is also a fact that more
quantity of onion was exported this year
as compared to the previous year from the
country; and
(d) if so, the quantity of exported onion
till January, 2007 and to what extent it is
lesser or more than the previous year?
Agricultural Extension Scheme
3194. SHRI RAMDAS AGARWAL:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have been
providing funds to States for implementing
Agricultural Extension Scheme;
(b) if so, whether any such scheme has
been introduced in Rajasthan; and
(c) if so, the allocation of funds made
therefor during the last three years, till
date?

Viable land holding
3195. SHRI  MATILAL SARKAR:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) the percentage of the number of
farmers having less than two acres of
cultivable land over the total number of
cultivable land holders, State and Union
Territory-wise;
(b) whether Government have made any
assessment about the minimum size of
holdings of cultivable land to be treated as
viable for a family to live by;
(c) if so, the size thereof; and
(d) the steps Government propose to
take for providing viable size of holding of
land to the farmers in the minimum?
Production of maize
3196. DR. M.A.M. RAMASWAMY:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) the total production of maize during
the last three years, year-wise;
(b) whether the All India Starch
Manufacturers, Association has demanded
a ban on export of maize;
(c) if so, the justification made by them
in their demand; and
(d) the reaction of the Central
Government in this regard?
Per hectare rice production
3197. SHRI S. ANBALAGAN: Will the
Minister of AGRICULTURE be pleased
to state:
(a) whether Government had taken note
that country's per hectare yield is very less
in rice production;
(b) if so, the details thereof during the
last three years particularly in comparison
to China, Japan and USA;
(c) whether Government propose to
initiate fresh steps to increase per hectre
yield of paddy/rice in the country as this
would ease the pressure on limited
availability of lands in the country; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Crop loss due to snowfall and rains in
northern India
3198. SHRI RAJKUMAR DHOOT:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that untimely
and unseasoned snow fall and rains in
northern India during March, 2007 has
destroyed crops in the areas;
(b) if so, the details thereof and the likely
loss of wheat and other cereals due to rains
and snowfall;
(c) whether sufficient stocks are
available to meet the shortfall; and
(d) if not, the steps proposed to be
taken to ensure full availability of
foodgrains during the coming months?
Promotion of Bt. cotton
3199. SHRI KARNENDU BHATTA-
CHARJEE: Will the Minister of
AGRICULTURE be pleased to state:
(a) whether some States have been
identified as holding special promise for
hybrid Bt. cotton;
(b) if so, what are these and to what
extent; and
(c) whether direction, if any, has been
issued to different States to promote hybrid
Bt. cotton?

742
Post Harvest Technology
3200. SHRIMATI N.P. DURGA: Will
the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) what are the aims and objectives of
Post Harvest Technology;
(b) how bringing the scheme of Post
Harvest Technology under Technology
Mission for Oil Seeds, Pulses and Maize
has helped in stepping up the production
of oil seeds, pulses and maize; and
(c) the details of indigenous
technologies developed through R&D and
the details of demonstration units set up?
Special products
3201. MS. SUSHILA TIRIYA: Will the
Minister of AGRICULTURE be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that there has
been disagreement over the number of farm
products/commodities that the country
would designate as special products; and
(b) if so, the reasons therefor?
Drop in seafood catch
3202. MS. MABEL REBELLO: Will
the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that there is an
alarming drop in seafood catch from the
western coast this year especially along
Kerala, Mangalore and Goa coasts;
(b) the reasons for this huge decline;
(c) what are the adverse affects on
seafood industry on the fishermen, boat
operators, ice factories, processing units,
freezing plants and transporters; and
(d) how Government would ameliorate
the sufferings of the above class and the
details thereof?
Retaining of ICAR Research Centre
at Kannara, Kerala
3203. SHRI K.E. ISMAIL: Will the
Minister of AGRICULTURE be pleased
to state:
(a) what is the basis on which
Government had proposed in 2001 through
ICAR that its Research Centre at Kannara
in Kerala would be phased out;
(b) whether there were requests from
many quarters, including from the State
Government that this Centre should be
retained and allowed to function better; and
(c) what is the status of this Centre
today and what is the response to the
requests for the Centre to be retained in
Kerala?
Rural indebtedness
3204. DR. GYAN PRAKASH
PILANIA:
SHRIMATI MAYA SINGH:
Will the Minister of AGRICUL TURE
be pleased to state:
(a) the dimension and prevalence of rural
indebtedness in India/States;
(b) the total number of suicides
committed by farmers due to indebtedness,
during the last ten years/till date, State-
wise and year-wise;
(c) the corrective measures taken by
Government in this regard;
(d) whether the National Commission
on Farmers has made any recommendations
in this context; and
(e) if so, the follow up action taken?

Tackling global warming effects on
agriculture
3205. SHRIMATI MOHSINA
KIDWAI: Will the Minister of
AGRICULTURE be pleased to state:
(a) whether ICAR or his Ministry has
taken up any study or research to find out
the impact of global warming on agriculture
in the country;
(b) if so, the details thereof and if not,
the reasons therefor;
(c) how much agriculture land has been
lost in the country due to global warming
and what would be its impact in the coming
future;
(d) whether erratic rainfall and frequent
floods and droughts which have destroyed
crops are the result of global warming; and
(e) if so, what strategy has been adopted
by ICAR to tackle this problem?
New system of cash plantation by the
Central Rice Research Institute
3206. SHRI B.J. PANDA:
MS. PRAMILA BOHIDAR:
Will the Minister of AGRICUL TURE
be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Central Rice Research
Institute has devised a new system of cash
plantation for rice growing farmers of
Orissa;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) how far this would help to increase
their income, generate additional
employment and restrict migration of the
farming community?
Poultry projects in Bihar
3207. SHRI TARIQ ANWAR: Will the
Minister of AGRICULTURE be pleased
to state:
(a) whether the Government of Bihar
has sent proposals for poultry projects
during the last two years;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the details of the funds allocated
therefor during that period?
Flood and drought loss in Kerala

PEEVEE: Will the Minister of
AGRICULTURE be pleased to state:
(a) the number of representations
received from the Government of Kerala
claiming compensation for agricultural loss
due to floods and droughts during the last
three years, year-wise;
(b) the details of assistance sought,
assistance approved and released in each
case;
(c) the status of pending
representations;
(d) whether Kerala Government has
also sought assistance for revival of
agriculture sector; and
(e) if so, the details thereof?
Mainstreaming the Agricultural
Technology Management Agency
model

SHRI GIREESH KUMAR
SANGHI:
Will the Minister of AGRICUL TURE
be pleased to state:
(a) how and where Government

sanctioned amount of Rs. 2260 million for
mainstreaming the Agricultural Technology
Management Agency model in 252 districts
during the Tenth Five Year Plan period,
have resulted in an envisaged improvement
for the benefit of farmers, especially the

(b) whether the streamlining has shown
any specific improvement, both being cost-

(c) if so, which are such districts in

Availability of foodgrains

BAL APTE:
SHRI SHREEGOPAL VYAS:
Will the Minister of AGRICUL TURE
be pleased to state:
(a) whether the per capita availability
of foodgrains has declined during the last
five years;
(b) if so, the details thereof, year-wise
and State-wise alongwith the reasons
therefor; and
(c) the remedial steps taken in this
regard?
Effect of global warming on
agriculture production
3211. SHRI JANARDHANA
POOJARY:
SHRI T.T.V. DHINAKARAN:
Will the Minister of AGRICUL TURE
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that global
warming is adversely affecting the
agriculture production in the country;
(b) if so, the details thereof with the
quantum of decline in the agricultural
produce during the last five years; year-
wise, State-wise, produce-wise ( i.e. rice,
wheat, sugarcane, oilseeds, etc.);
(c) whether Government propose to
conduct a study on the impact of global
warming on India's agriculture and to take
remedial measures; and
(d) if so, the details thereof and if not,
the reasons therefor?
Agricultural SEZs

RAO: Will the Minister of
AGRICULTURE be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have
formulated Agricultural Special Economic

SEZs scheme;

be acquired for creating industries, sugar

would be formed; and
(e) the reasons for this unusual concept?

LAXMAN NAIK: Will the Minister of
AGRICULTURE be pleased to state:
(a) whether schemes for agricultural
mechanisation are in force in Goa;
(b) the essential features of the schemes;
(c) the projects undertaken/
implemented under the schemes during the
last five years in the State; and

(d) the details of financial assistance
granted to the State during that period,
year-wise?

CHATURVEDI:
SHRI MOTILAL VORA:
Will the Minister of AGRICUL TURE
be pleased to state:
(a) whether 50 lakh hectares of
additional land would be required to meet
the foodgrain and oilseed requirements of
rapidly growing population;

hectares of additional land for agriculture

land

SHRI MOTILAL VORA:
SHRI SATYAVRAT
CHATURVEDI:
Will the Minister of AGRICUL TURE
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that chemical
manure has converted the fertile land into a
barren land in the States;
(b) if so, the details of fertile land so
affected during the last three years,
State-wise and year-wise;
(c) the steps being taken/proposed to
be taken by Government to convert the
barren land into fertile land for more
agriculture produce; and
(d) the details of other steps being taken
by Government to convert such barren land
into fertile land again and making farmers
aware about excessive use of chemical
fertilizers?
Production and consumption of pulses
3216. SHRI T.S. BAJWA: Will the
Minister of AGRICULTURE be pleased
to state:
(a) the details of production and
consumption of pulses in the country

(b) whether the domestic production is
sufficient to meet the requirements; and
(c) if not, how Government propose to
meet the situation?
Weather based insurance

RAIAH: Will the Minister of
AGRICULTURE be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government propose to
offer weather based crop insurance scheme
for farmers;
(b) if so, whether the scheme would be
operated on an actuarial basis with an
element of subsidy;
(c) if so, what would be the component
of the subsidy;
(d) in which States the scheme would
be implemented and how many small
farmers are expected to be covered;

insurance company has been made the nodal

Enhancing productivity
3218. SHRIMATI PREMA
CARIAPPA:
SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA:
